tasks.short: Monitor cardiac patients using electrocardiography devices

steps.what: Verify the patient and fit and check the electrocardiography monitoring device
Monitor cardiac traces and patient condition and distinguish recording artefacts
Respond to concerning findings and coordinate clinical review

tasks.design: Retain device fitting, trace review and clinical response with qualified staff, using {OTHER}, the existing electrocardiography monitoring device. Existing signal acquisition and alarms are baseline runtime and earn no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recorded signals require checks against patient condition and recording quality.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest supplies no validated cardiac-monitoring change for this task.
tasks.still_hard: Artefacts, intermittent events and urgent deterioration.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist recognises clinical concern and escalates within local scope.
tasks.altitude: No change to monitoring work or clinical authority.

evidence.claim: The scenario retains cardiac trace review and response; no respiratory-role monitoring saving is established by the digest.

assumptions: Boundary covers therapist setup, monitoring attention and response; unattended device recording is excluded from human baseline hours.

Therapist verifies patient identity, order and signal quality in s1's30 hours and interprets observed findings in s2. The existing device produces the trace from its electrodes; no free structured clinical event label is assumed.
Local clinical scope and device procedures govern action. No new tool or upkeep is added, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Local monitoring responsibilities and device type
Existing alarm and trace review procedures
research_questions: Which monitoring actions require human attention despite existing recording and alarms?

already_counted.description: Setup, trace review and clinical response

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; existing automated recording is not counted as human effort or a new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend high-risk infant deliveries and provide neonatal respiratory care

steps.what: Confirm neonatal respiratory responsibilities and check delivery-room equipment readiness
Attend high-risk or caesarian deliveries and assess neonatal respiratory needs
Provide indicated neonatal respiratory care and coordinate the clinical handoff

tasks.design: Keep equipment checks, delivery attendance and neonatal care with the clinical team. Existing protocols in {DOCS} support practice; no automated readiness or respiratory-treatment decision is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Care depends on immediate newborn condition and coordinated physical intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's documentation tools do not replace delivery attendance or neonatal care.
tasks.still_hard: Rapidly changing physiology and time-critical team actions.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist supplies skilled respiratory support and clear clinical communication.
tasks.altitude: No change in attendance time or neonatal care authority.

reach.task: Prepare and support neonatal delivery care

evidence.claim: Delivery attendance and indicated neonatal respiratory care remain skilled physical work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers therapist delivery preparation, attendance and care; delivery scheduling, other clinicians' labour and separate charting are excluded.

Therapist and team establish roles and physically verify equipment in s1's20 hours. The therapist assesses respiratory needs in s2's50 hours; no pre-existing structured readiness or treatment flag is assumed.
Shares represent a workload mix including deliveries needing care. Local authorised practice governs care. No new system or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Delivery workload mix and local clinical scope
research_questions: Does separate charting contain avoidable work without reducing delivery attendance?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; no reduction to equipment verification, skilled attendance or neonatal care is proposed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: These monitoring and neonatal care tasks retain their skilled clinical time.
reach: Learn recording-quality checks with cardiovascular technologists
Practise neonatal handoffs with delivery nurses
role.ambitious_version: A respiratory therapist who provides reliable monitoring and neonatal support within a coordinated clinical team.
